_about: THE DESK VOCABULARY (operator idea, 2026-10-18): one shared set of codes every worker -- training and live -- writes and reads, so a post, an alert plan or a journal note says exactly what it means in a few tokens, and nobody re-explains a setup in prose. `python3 tools/vocab.py index` lists every code, `lookup CODE ...` defines them, `find WORDS` searches. Setup records come from the training ledger (28 closed paper trades, Dec 2024 - May 2025): thin, one regime, mostly gold -- hypotheses with a track record, not proof.

grammar.post: SYM CODE SIDE @entry SL x TP y | trig | inv | note   e.g. XAUUSD S1 BUY @3302 SL 3294 TP 3320 | T-HOLD 3300 M15x2 | INV H1<3290 | TREND-UP ACCEPT>PDH
grammar.dismiss: SYM DISMISS code[,code] | note   e.g. XAGEUR DISMISS A5,A4 | same metals move as XAGUSD, rollover pop
grammar.alert --why: CODE SIDE @level SL x TP y | trig | inv   e.g. S2 SELL @3290 SL 3302 TP 3266 | T-REJECT 3290 M5 | INV M15>3305
grammar.rule: codes first, prose only for what no code says; prices are real levels from the bars; tf after a level is the bar the trigger is judged on

S1.name: ACCEPT-CONT
S1.def: Continuation after acceptance above a broken level (mirror for shorts). H1/H4 HH-HL; price broke a SWING-H and HELD above it 2h+ in a tight CONSOL that never lost the level.
S1.entry: inside/at the edge of the consolidation, not after a fresh IMPULSE away
S1.stop: under the consolidation low / the broken level
S1.record: 6 gold longs 6W ~+12R (Jan-Feb 2025 uptrend); same family lost 5x when entered mid-pullback before the HL (A2) or at a RANGE-H

S2.name: FAILED-CTR
S2.def: Failed counter-move in a trend: a bounce (downtrend) or dip (uptrend) runs into a prior breakdown/breakout zone and FAILS -- LH (or HL) printed and a closed M15/M5 bar REJECTs back in the trend direction.
S2.record: 3W (USDJPY +0.54R, US100 +2.25R, gold short +1.42R); lost when sold before the bounce had failed (A2)

S3.name: EVENT-RETRACE
S3.def: A news/event SPIKE fully retraced, then M15 HL (or LH) away from the spike extreme.
S3.entry: after the structure forms, never during the spike

S4.name: BREAK-ACCEPT
S4.def: Breakout with acceptance: price breaks a SHELF or a prior SPIKE extreme and ACCEPTs there (several hours of closes beyond it, no return inside).
S4.stop: back inside, under the shelf / acceptance base
S4.record: 2W (US100 +1.94R, gold +1.97R); 1L on a FLAG box taken without the acceptance

A1.name: CHASE
A1.def: Entering an IMPULSE or SPIKE that already ran 3+ ATR(M15) from its base with no pause, pullback or acceptance. A move that just happened is not A1 by itself: judge it by the setup code it fits (a break that holds is S4, a failed counter-move is S2).
A1.instead: ALERT at the RETEST of the breakout base

A2.name: EARLY-PULLBACK
A2.def: Entering a pullback before it printed its HL/LH -- the counter-move is still running.
A2.instead: wait for the HL/LH and a closed REJECT bar (S2), or ALERT on T-REJECT

A3.name: PACING
A3.def: An entry whose real reason is 'the account needs a traded day', with no setup code matching.
A3.instead: a small trade only if a setup code fits; otherwise an ALERT plan

A4.name: THIN/GAP
A4.def: Thin-hour or rollover entries, or a move that is only a session-open / rollover GAP.
A4.instead: DISMISS, or wait for the window's liquid hours

A5.name: CORRELATED
A5.def: One move counted several times (gold in USD and EUR; silver USD/EUR; US100/US500/US30 together; oil WTI/Brent).
A5.instead: read one, mark the rest DISMISS A5
A5.record: scouts kept re-reading the same move

HH.name: higher high
HH.def: a swing high above the previous swing high

HL.name: higher low
HL.def: a swing low above the previous swing low

LH.name: lower high
LH.def: a swing high below the previous swing high

LL.name: lower low
LL.def: a swing low below the previous swing low

BOS.name: break of structure
BOS.def: a close beyond the last swing in the trend direction

CHOCH.name: change of character
CHOCH.def: the first close beyond the last swing AGAINST the trend (first LL in an uptrend, first HH in a downtrend)

IMPULSE.name: impulse
IMPULSE.def: consecutive same-direction bars with ranges well above the recent average, little overlap

PULLBACK.name: pullback
PULLBACK.def: a counter-move inside a trend that has not broken the last HL/LH

CONSOL.name: consolidation
CONSOL.def: overlapping bars in a tight band after a move; the band's high/low are its edges

FLAG.name: flag
FLAG.def: a small counter-sloped CONSOL after an IMPULSE

SHELF.name: shelf
SHELF.def: a flat area with several equal highs (or lows) acting as a ceiling (floor)

SPIKE.name: spike
SPIKE.def: one or two outsized bars, often news; EVT-X is its extreme

SWEEP.name: liquidity sweep
SWEEP.def: a wick beyond an obvious level (PDH, SWING-H, RANGE-H) that closes back inside

ACCEPT.name: acceptance
ACCEPT.def: closes beyond a level held for N bars (write ACCEPT>level tf xN)

REJECT.name: rejection
REJECT.def: a bar that trades through a level and closes back on the original side

RETEST.name: retest
RETEST.def: price returning to a broken level from the new side

GAP.name: gap
GAP.def: the open far from the previous close: session open, rollover, weekend, news

TREND-UP.name: uptrend
TREND-UP.def: H1 (or the tf named) prints HH and HL; price above the last HL

TREND-DN.name: downtrend
TREND-DN.def: H1 (or the tf named) prints LH and LL; price below the last LH

RANGE.name: range
RANGE.def: price oscillating between a RANGE-H and RANGE-L for several swings

CHOP.name: chop
CHOP.def: overlapping bars, no clean swings, no edge

EXHAUSTED.name: exhausted
EXHAUSTED.def: a move 3+ ATR(M15) from its base without a pullback; continuation entries here are A1

SWING-H.name: swing high
SWING-H.def: a bar high with lower highs on both sides (state the tf)

SWING-L.name: swing low
SWING-L.def: a bar low with higher lows on both sides (state the tf)

PDH.name: prior day high
PDH.def: the previous Prague trading day's high

PDL.name: prior day low
PDL.def: the previous Prague trading day's low

RN.name: round number
RN.def: a price ending in 00/50 (or 000/500 on indices)

EVT-X.name: event extreme
EVT-X.def: the far end of a news SPIKE

T-TOUCH.name: touch
T-TOUCH.def: any trade at the level -- paper.py alert --when touch (refused next to price: that is a poll)

T-CLOSE.name: close beyond
T-CLOSE.def: a closed bar of the named tf beyond the level: T-CLOSE>3302 M15 -- paper.py alert --when close --tf M15

T-HOLD.name: hold
T-HOLD.def: N consecutive closes beyond the level: T-HOLD 3300 M15x2 -- paper.py alert --when hold --tf M15 --bars 2

T-REJECT.name: rejection trigger
T-REJECT.def: a bar through the level that closes back: T-REJECT 3290 M5 -- paper.py alert --when reject --tf M5

INV.name: invalidation
INV.def: the condition that kills the plan: INV H1<3290 (a close of that tf beyond it)

DISMISS.name: dismiss
DISMISS.def: nothing to do; give the code(s) why (A1-A5, CHOP, GAP, EXHAUSTED)

NOW.name: trade now
NOW.def: a clean entry right now: hand to the trader with CODE SIDE SL TP

ALERT.name: alert
ALERT.def: a real setup whose entry is still to come: paper.py alert at the level, plan in the grammar

WATCH.name: watch
WATCH.def: forming but not plannable yet; post it so the next scout or decision turn starts from it

R.name: R
R.def: the entry-to-stop distance; 2R = a target twice that far

BE.name: break-even
BE.def: stop moved to the entry price

SL@S.name: stop at structure
SL@S.def: a stop placed beyond a named structure level, never an arbitrary distance
